column1: # Players whose format needs more than a 68000. One line per player.
# UADE emulates an 020, so a player can depend on 020 behaviour -- chiefly
# misaligned longword access, which is legal there and an ADDRESS ERROR on a
# 68000 -- and nobody upstream would notice. On a real A500 that is a guru, so
# a build that targets 68000 with such a format must be REFUSED rather than
# `source` says who decided, because these are not all measurable: a device
# failure tells you THIS player faults on a 68000, not whether the format was
# ever meant to run there. The owner's scene knowledge settles that, and it is
# the authority for the rows marked `owner`.

column4: owner: not an A500-compatible format. Matches the measurement -- ADRE (address error, misaligned longword) at 0x000161A0 in call_check_module on a 68000, plays under uade123, which emulates an 020.

measured 2026-11-21: ADRE at the player's own check scan (current.uadeplayer code offset 0x168, cmpi.w #$4e75,(a0) with a0 stepped by 1 from the module base, so a0=0x23001 faults) on a 68000 for anarchy.sid1; plays under uade123 (020).

column1: # --- formats the REFERENCE implementation cannot play with the modules we have.

column4: all four Modland TFMX ST modules: uade123 says "module check failed". Atari ST TFMX; the mdat. half alone is not enough.
